wars.outcome: Treaty of Oliva, 3 May 1660: Poland 'gave up most of Livonia, including Riga, and kept only Latgale'; John II Casimir renounces the Swedish throne; Ducal Prussia sovereign by Labiau (20 November 1656), Wehlau and Bromberg (6 November 1657).
wars.note: Warsaw taken in 1655, retaken 1 July 1656 and again 28-30 July (Swedish-Brandenburg victory); taken on 17 May 1657 by 'the Swedes, Cossacks, and Transylvanians'; Treaty of Radnot (8 December 1656) proposes a partition of the Commonwealth. Population loss 'approximately one third'.

wars.name: Polish–Ottoman War (1672–1676)

zones.text: Podole, Bracław and part of Kiev voivodeships

wars.outcome: Peace of Buczacz (October 1672) cedes Podole, Bracław and part of Kiev voivodeship and a tribute of 22,000 ducats; the Sejm does not ratify; Khotyn (11 November 1673) is a victory; Żurawno (1676) ends the tribute and returns Bila Tserkva and Pavoloch, the Ottomans keeping about two thirds of the 1672 gains.
wars.note: Kamieniec Podolski is taken in August 1672 and not recovered in this war.

wars.name: Great Turkish War
wars.outcome: Treaty of Karlowitz, 26 January 1699: the Commonwealth recovers Podolia and gives back captured Moldavian fortresses.
wars.note: Only the Karlowitz page was opened: the war's earlier years (the Holy League of 1684 and the Polish campaigns) are not on it; the 1698 campaign did not take Kamianets.

wars.name: Great Northern War
wars.outcome: Charles XII invades Poland-Lithuania (1702), a Warsaw Confederation elects Leszczyński (1704, crowned 1705); Altranstädt (October 1706) dethrones Augustus II; after Poltava (1709) Augustus 'regained the Polish throne'; Nystad (1721) is between Russia and Sweden. A formal Swedish-Polish peace came only in 1732.
wars.note: The Commonwealth's land change is the 1706-1709 interval of Pro-Swedish Poland; no border moved at Nystad. The page does not mention the Silent Sejm (1717).

wars.name: Russo-Polish War of 1792

zones.text: the land Russia occupied and Cliopatria removes in 1792

wars.outcome: Russian forces invade; the Targowica magnates fight the pro-constitution forces ('War in Defense of the Constitution'); the Second Partition (23 January 1793) annexes 307,300 km2.
wars.note: The page gives no month for the Targowica Confederation and no extent for the occupation.

wars.name: Kościuszko Uprising
wars.outcome: The uprising 'began' in 1794; the Third Partition treaty (24 October 1795) divides the remaining 215,000 km2 and Stanisław August abdicates (25 November 1795).
wars.note: The page gives no month and no battles for the uprising.

certainty.note: The eastern and southern frontiers (Muscovy, the Wild Fields, Moldavia, the Crimean khanate) are approximate; sharp lines only at the Truce of Jam Zapolski (1582) for Livonia and Polotsk, the Truce of Deulino (1619), the Truce of Altmark (1629) and the Polyanovka treaty (1634) where the pages name towns.

Fixed by treaty: Andrusovo (1667) with Russia, Buchach/Żurawno (1672/1676) and Karlowitz (1699) with the Ottomans, Oliva (1660) with Sweden and Brandenburg-Prussia; the south-eastern steppe edge (Zaporozhia, Podolian borderland) stays soft.
The partitions of 1772, 1793 and 1795 draw treaty lines with area figures; the Ottoman frontier on the Dniester is as before.
